In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of immunocytochemical methods to detect the expression of P-glycoproteins in tumour cell lines and tissues.
the development of monoclonal antibodies which are able to distinguish between the different forms of P-glycoproteins and the development of an immunocytochemical staining procedure for their use.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monoclonal antibody 265/F4 is the most specific antibody for the detection of P-glycoproteins in murine cell lines.
C219, MRk 16, JSb-1 and 26S/F4 all recognise the P-glycoproteins, but that the last antibody appears to recognise a distinct form.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mdr1 gene family is not only expressed in the liver and kidney, but in a wide variety of tissues, and that the expression of the mdr1 genes in tumour cell lines can be detected by the use of the 265/F4 monoclonal antibody.
the monoclonal antibody 265/F4 is the only one of the four tested antibodies that recognises mdr1b, but not mdr1a.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of mdr-1a and mrd-1b genes are not necessarily correlated in all the mouse tumor cell line, and this may be due to differential regulation of the expression of these genes in different tumor cell lines.
the mdr1 gene family is not a simple one gene family, but is a complex of at least two different genes.
there are at least three different isoforms of P-gp in mice, and that the mdr1 and mdr2 genes are expressed in different organs in the mouse.
